thread.title: Broadcom: Shares Must Be Owned Now - Broadcom Limited (NASDAQ:AVGO)

author: Shmulik Karpf
title: Broadcom: Shares Must Be Owned Now - Broadcom Limited (NASDAQ:AVGO)
text:
My high conviction investment thesis on Broadcom ( AVGO ) is based on three success pillars. The first pillar is revenue growth, accompanied by a significant rise in free cash flow. The second pillar is shareholder friendliness - how the company treats its shareholders. The third pillar, as in with every investment, is the current compelling valuation of shares.
Revenues And Cash Flow - Rapid Growth Revenue growth is important in all industries, but especially in the tech sector. You see, a tech company that is unable to grow revenues at a reasonable pace is likely losing out to rivals. In that sense, Broadcom definitely passes the revenue growth test with flying colors.
In its most recent quarter, Broadcom generated net revenues in the amount of 5$ billion, an increase of 20 percent from 4.19$ billion in the same quarter last year. The company's growth is well balanced between its different divisions. Wireless generated 1.3$ billion in revenues, up 13 percent year over year, and that's despite some weakness from shipments to Apple ( AAPL ).
Wired Infrastructure recorded 2.3$ billion in revenues, up 9 percent compared to the same quarter last year, supported by a recovery in broadband spend. Enterprise Storage generated 1.16$ billion in revenues, up 17 percent quarter over quarter, mainly attributed to higher level of spend by the IT sector.
But Broadcom doesn't only grow revenues. It also generates free cash flow at a rapid pace. In the most recent quarter, Broadcom generated free cash flow of 2.12$ billion or 42 percent of net revenue. That's a highly remarkable revenue conversion rate.
Shareholder Friendly Management isn't sitting idle on that pile of cash. It is putting it to good use, which basically means - creating shareholder value by accretive M&A activity, high dividends and a commitment to buy back massive amounts of shares.
In its most recent quarterly report , Broadcom disclosed that it had bought 6.4 million shares during the past quarter, with total investment of 1.5$ billion - and that's just in the past quarter alone. This recent buyback is an implementation of a greater share buyback program, in a total of 12$ billion, announced back in April. I also expect the 7$ dividend per share to increase to 9$ per share next year.
With buybacks and dividends on the rise, I believe that shareholders are expected to receive roughly 20$ billion back from Broadcom, over the next two years. Now, that's a staggering sum.
Valuation Is A Screaming "BUY" Due to current headwinds from the ongoing trade war with China, the semiconductor industry in selling on the cheap. Specifically, Broadcom is trading at a lowly twelve times next year's earnings. This represents one of the lowest valuations in the company's history. Especially notable is the contrast between the gradual rise in revenue and earnings per share (white and green line, respectively) versus the recent sharp decline in valuation (brown line). This is my favorite setup for entry.
Caught Between Value And Growth I believe that the main reason why shares are so incredibly cheap has to do with perception. You see, Broadcom is somewhat of a mixed bag - it isn't your typical growth stock and it isn't a classic value stock either. I believe that this somewhat complex perception has distanced both types of investors away from this fantastic company. Let me explain.
Operating in a mature industry, generating mountains of cash, and trading at low double-digit earnings multiple - Broadcom has traditionally been perceived as a value stock. But things have changed dramatically a few months back when Broadcom had announced a takeover offer for Qualcomm ( QCOM ). Although this offer failed to materialize, due to a variety of unrelated reasons, I believe that the mere offer scared many traditional value investors.
You see, Qualcomm is a big whale to swallow, so to successfully complete the transaction, Broadcom was willing to take on a massive amount of debt, something that would hinder its balance sheet and would surely lead to a downgrade by one of the leading rating agencies. This was enough to scare away traditional value centered investors focusing on safety of capital.
On the other hand, Broadcom isn't your typical growth stock either. The semiconductor industry is a relatively mature one, and Broadcom hasn't been able to generate double-digit revenue growth, which is something growth investors normally require. So, there it is - shares of Broadcom are caught between value and growth, looking for owners.
My Takeaway Broadcom is a leading company in the semiconductor sector. It gushes cash flow, grows revenue at a rapid pace, and treats its shareholders very well. Finally, shares are trading at a great price due to the turmoil surrounding the trade war. Broadcom is a share that must be owned.
 AVGO.
